items.title: Mind your head: Entropic Brain, irruption theory and the intelligibility problem
items.summary: Abstract The entropic brain hypothesis (EBH) and irruption theory (IT) are two recent frameworks to investigate consciousness by examining neural entropy. items.title: Practical limitations on robustness and scalability of quantum Internet
items.summary: Abstract The realization of a desirably functional quantum Internet is hindered by fundamental and practical challenges such as high loss during transmission of quantum systems, decoherence due to interaction with the environment, and fragility of quantum states under measurement. items.title: Quantum resources for everlasting communication security
items.summary: Abstract Quantum cryptography provides communication with everlasting security—a property unattainable by classical or post-quantum cryptography. Traditionally, quantum cryptography proclaims everlasting security by relying on principles such as no-cloning theorem, Bell inequalities, or the uncertainty principle, along with the standard assumption that legitimate users have no control over the communication channel.

items.title: The quantum-ready college: quantum technologies as an industry shift and how higher education should prepare
items.summary: Purpose This paper examines the emerging industry shift in which quantum technologies are evolving from isolated scientific breakthroughs into full-scale innovation ecosystems that will reshape higher education. items.title: Quantum Searching and Optimization Algorithms: A Comprehensive Guide

items.summary: Anomaly-based malware detectors learn what benign files look like and flag deviations. Generative approaches to this problem can make use of a "latent" or "prior" data representation, which is often chosen to be a Gaussian distribution.

items.summary: The Hard Problem of Consciousness and Qualia in the Acta Universi Hypothesis Abstract (EN) The hard problem of consciousness asks why physical processes are accompanied by subjective experience. This paper offers a reformulation of the problem within the Acta Universi (AU) hypothesis—a speculative informational-entropic ontology.

items.title: A glutamatergic projection from the central medial thalamic nucleus to the red nucleus regulates states of consciousness during sevoflurane anesthesia in mice
items.summary: General anesthetics like sevoflurane are clinically essential, yet the neural circuits governing their induction of unconsciousness and recovery remain incompletely defined. Here, we show the potential involvement of the vesicular glutamate transporter 2 (Vglut2)-expressing glutamatergic neurons in the central medial thalamus (CMT Vglut2 neurons) in modulation states of consciousness under sevoflurane anesthesia.

items.title: From unimodal to multimodal deep physiological signal analysis in healthcare: A survey of models, fusion and explainability
items.summary: Physiological signal analysis supports objective assessment of emotion, stress, pain, and disease progression in healthcare systems. Early research focused mainly on unimodal signals, which perform well in controlled settings but are often affected by noise, limited contextual information and reduced generalisability.

items.title: Patient-specific factors are associated with distinct brain network connectivity in disorders of consciousness
items.summary: Disorders of consciousness (DoC) arise from diverse etiologies and exhibit substantial clinical heterogeneity, including variations in patient age and time since injury. However, how these clinical characteristics relate to large-scale brain network connectivity and are associated with consciousness levels and functional outcomes remains poorly understood.

items.title: Spin-Based Quantum Information Processing in Cytoskeletal Filaments Using Nucleoside Phosphates
items.summary: Abstract Phosphorus nuclear spins are candidates for quantum information processing in biological matter because 31P is a spin-1/2nucleus without an electric quadrupole moment, although coherence remains environment-dependent. Recent work rangesfrom theoretical proposals based on phosphate ions and Posner molecules to experimental demonstrations of room-temperaturequantum logic in adenosine diphosphate.

items.title: Testing non-classical gravitational phase dynamics under strong dephasing
items.summary: Whether gravity must be quantum is often approached by asking whether two masses can become entangled through their mutual gravitational interaction. In practice, the weak interaction competes with environmental decoherence, so the final state may contain no entanglement even when the underlying gravitational phase remains coherent.

items.title: Quantum AI for E-Commerce: From Theory to Practice
items.summary: This book offers a multidisciplinary and business-focused exploration of AI and computing, highlighting their potential impact on digital commerce, entrepreneurship,and innovation. It critically examines the shift towards data-driven technologies as organisations strive to enhance value creation, operational efficiency, and customer experience.

items.title: Fixed-preparation short-time reconstruction of class-D BdG endpoint masses
items.summary: In one-dimensional class-D superconductors, the relative signs of the Bogoliubov--de Gennes (BdG) masses at particle--hole-invariant momenta fix the bulk $\mathbb Z_2$ invariant. Band energies and transition-frequency peak locations alone cannot determine these signs.

items.title: Distinguishing gagging, nausea, retching, and vomiting: A multidimensional psychophysiological framework
items.summary: Gagging, nausea, retching, and vomiting are often reported together clinically, but differ in their triggers, subjective features, motor organization, and relation to expulsion. This narrative review compares them using human studies, research on airway protection, and animal models of emesis.

items.title: Operationally induced preferred basis in unitary quantum mechanics
items.summary: Abstract The preferred-basis problem remains under unitary system–apparatus dynamics, whereas measurements have mutually exclusive outcomes. The present framework places basis selection in the complete preparation–measurement arrangement.

items.title: Universal quantum gate set for multimode Schrödinger cat states stabilized by nonlocal dissipation engineering
items.summary: Schrödinger cat states provide a hardware-efficient platform for bosonic quantum error correction by encoding logical information in protected manifolds of harmonic oscillators. While previous work has demonstrated the dissipative stabilization of multi-mode Schrödinger cat states as robust quantum memories, a framework for universal quantum computation has remained unavailable.

items.title: Anesthesia via Dissociative Overload: A Unified Theoretical Framework Linking DMT and Ketamine Through Sigma-1 Convergence, Entropic Saturation, and Workspace Flooding
items.summary: General anesthesia has long been understood as a unitary phenomenon driven by neural suppression — a reduction in cortical activity, entropy, and complexity that renders the brain unable to sustain conscious processing. Yet two structurally and pharmacologically distinct compounds, N,N-Dimethyltryptamine (DMT) and ketamine, produce clinical unresponsiveness while maintaining or increasing cortical complexity, a pattern fundamentally incompatible with the suppression paradigm.

items.title: Nonlocality as a benchmarking tool for quantum processors
items.summary: Abstract Benchmarking quantum processors is a central task in every roadmap aimed at quantum advantage. Here, we discuss a benchmarking protocol based on the violation of the Svetlichny inequality, which is designed to simulate genuine multipartite nonlocality.

items.title: Qualia Is Not a Pseudoproblem: A Response to Balconi et al. (2026), 'The End of Qualia'
items.summary: A response to Balconi et al.'s (2026) Frontiers in Psychology editorial proposing that qualia be retired as a pseudoproblem in Kuhn's sense. The letter argues that the collection the editorial introduces does not support its eliminative frame; that a malformed question has never licensed abandoning the phenomenon it names; and that first-person report remains the foundation on which pain science, affective neuroscience, and clinical measurement were built — the reports came first, and the instruments followed them.

items.title: Adaptive sensing beyond non-adaptive information limits: End-to-end co-design of geometry, policy, and inference
items.summary: Inverse design has transformed vast physical parameter spaces into a substrate for emergent functionality, raising the tantalizing prospect of relocating intelligence from the digital domain into the physical world itself. Nowhere is this prospect more consequential than in sensing, where the analog-to-digital interface imposes a fundamental bottleneck: information not captured by the hardware is irrevocably lost to any downstream algorithm.

items.title: Preserved consciousness as a diagnostic pitfall: a probable case of tramadol-induced serotonergic toxicity with isolated neuromuscular symptoms in an adolescent after general anesthesia
items.summary: Serotonin syndrome (SS) typically presents with altered mental status, autonomic dysfunction, and neuromuscular abnormalities. We report an atypical case of perioperative tramadol-induced serotonergic toxicity in an adolescent characterized by isolated neuromuscular symptoms with completely preserved consciousness and stable autonomic function, challenging the established paradigm that altered mental status and hyperthermia are obligatory for diagnosis.

items.summary: Superconducting quantum circuits are among the most promising platforms for quantum computing, but their design remains a complex inverse problem, requiring the identification of circuit architectures and physical parameters capable of reproducing a desired quantum response. items.summary: The second-order Rényi entropy is one of the most important quantities used for characterizing the entanglement structure of states prepared in quantum many-body experiments. With access to qubit projective measurement data, it can be estimated via a protocol in which repeated measurements are taken after each of a set of random local unitary operations is applied to the quantum state.

items.title: Dynamical Light-Matter Coupling with Protected Superconducting Oscillators
items.summary: Superconducting circuits hosting long-lived bosonic modes are an excellent platform for emulating the dynamics of light and matter and exploiting them for quantum information processing. The space of accessible dynamics is greatly extended by introducing the frequency tunability of artificial atoms, whereby the interactions with the light field of a microwave cavity can be modified on demand.

items.title: Quantum Open Effective Field Theory: anomalous decoherence
items.summary: We study decoherence of a scalar field coupled to ``anomalous'' environments with critical behavior with the Schwinger-Keldysh including the influence functional, and the quantum master equation (QME) up to second order in the coupling. The Schwinger-Keldysh formulation yields a Langevin equation and the Lindblad (QME) includes \emph{time dependent rates} allowing to study transient dynamics.

items.title: Pilot-waves and copilot-particles: A nonstochastic approach to objective wavefunction collapse
items.summary: We propose an extension to Schrödinger’s equation that incorporates macroscopic measurement-induced wavefunction collapse. We find that a hybrid between two leading approaches, the Bohm-de Broglie pilot-wave and objective collapse theories, accomplishes this goal in accordance with Born’s rule.

items.title: A Quantum-Classical Surrogate Model for the Collision Operator of the Lattice Boltzmann Method
items.summary: We introduce a hybrid approach utilising a quantum machine learning surrogate model to approximate the non-linear collision dynamics of the LBM. It offloads the non-unitary operations that challenge pure quantum solvers.

items.title: Alzheimer's Disease: Mechanisms and Therapeutic Advances
items.summary: Alzheimer's disease (AD) is a devastating neurodegenerative condition accompanied by widespread central nervous system damage and complex networked pathogenesis spanning molecular, cellular, and systemic dimensions. Existing studies tend to focus on individual pathological cascades or monotherapeutic approaches, while overlooking the intrinsic crosstalk among protein pathology, neuroinflammation, metabolic dysfunction, and gut-brain axis imbalance, with insufficient systematic integration of nonpharmacological…

items.title: Galantamine for routine neuromuscular block reversal and treatment of emergence delirium in children after ENT surgery: a retrospective observational study
items.summary: New work indexed under “Galantamine for routine neuromuscular block reversal and treatment of emergence delirium in children after ENT surgery: a retrospective observational study.” The source did not provide an abstract; read the original before evaluating its claims.

items.title: Quantum Knowledge Distillation: State-of-the-art, Applications and Open Problems
items.summary: Knowledge distillation transfers predictions, representations, or other supervisory information between learning models and is increasingly investigated in quantum machine learning. Its applications extend beyond compression to cross-architecture transfer, circuit approximation, distributed learning, and classical deployment of models trained using quantum-derived supervision.

items.title: Taming a macroscopic free mass through continuous quantum measurement
items.summary: The free particle is the most elementary dynamical system in quantum mechanics. Despite remarkable progress in quantum control of increasingly massive solid-state mechanical oscillators, the analogous control of the free-particle counterpart has remained elusive.

items.title: Structured Representation

items.title: Comprehensive Study and Applications of Quantum Computing for Internet of Things
items.summary: A subfield of computer science known as “quantum computing” uses concepts from quantum theory. Atomic and subatomic matter and energy behavior are described by the theory of quantum mechanics.

items.title: Managing Emerging Technologies for Financial Transformation: An Integrative TAM–DOI–RBV Framework
items.summary: Advances in quantum computing and AR/VR are transforming financial management and consumer interactions, yet their integration continues to face challenges related to adoption, security, and organizational readiness. This study aims to analyze the integration of these technologies into financial management and examine their implications for organizational purpose, financial management strategies, and consumer behavior.
items.source: Jurnal Aplikasi Manajemen Ekonomi dan Bisnis

items.title: Ageing and anaesthetic sensitivity: the role of inflammaging in the vulnerable surgical brain
items.summary: Ageing surgical patients demonstrate increased vulnerability to anaesthetic agents, including heightened sensitivity, reduced drug requirements, and delayed emergence, and they are also at increased risk of postoperative complications such as delirium and haemodynamic instability. These phenomena are only partially understood and have traditionally been attributed to the global functional decline associated with ageing.

items.title: Reproducibility package for: Spectral envelopes, intra-shell fluctuations, and steady-state entropy in isolated quantum systems
items.summary: Numerical source code and deposited tables for the article Spectral envelopes, intra-shell fluctuations, and steady-state entropy in isolated quantum systems by Zhiqiang Huang and Qing-yu Cai. Package (ZZZ4-code-v1.0.zip): 93 scripts in six groups — code/solver (exact diagonalization of the Ising chains with ITensor, and the entropy of the dephased state), code/shells (shell intensity law, the non-Gaussianity q(λ), width and shift), code/closure (the self-consistent closure, its finite-width ladder, the four-cell…

items.title: Quantum Advantage in Sensing and Imaging through Coherent Nuisance Suppression
items.summary: Many sensing and imaging problems must contend with unknown nuisance parameters such as aberrations, background fields, and drift, and the cost of removing these noise sources can dominate the sample budget. In contrast to classical receivers, a quantum receiver can processes samples jointly to directly access observables in which common nuisance is suppressed.

items.title: Unruh-DeWitt detectors in a delocalized massive shell
items.summary: We construct a model for the response of a detector to vacuum fluctuations inside a massive hollow shell in a superposition of positions. The delocalized source mass gives rise to a superposition of spacetime geometries and their associated vacuum fluctuations.
keywords: quantum field theory in curved spacetime

items.title: Modelos de metadatos para experimentos en circuitos cuánticos: un mapeo sistemático
items.summary: Statistical reproducibility in Noisy Intermediate-Scale Quantum Computing (NISQ) is hindered by hardware variability and by the lack of metadata management practices able to capture calibration, compilation decisions, and data provenance. Although these elements are essential for experimental traceability, the evidence on how they are modeled and operationalized remains scattered.

items.title: Entanglement Allocation for Quantum Integrated Sensing and Communication
items.summary: Jointly supporting communication and distributed sensing over a shared, limited pool of entanglement resources is an attractive prospect for future quantum networks. We develop a network-level quantum integrated sensing and communication (Q-ISAC) framework in which a quantum base station dynamically allocates elementary Bell pairs between communication users and distributed sensing.

items.title: Parton wave functions, density matrices and entropy in DGLAP evolution
items.summary: Parton multiplicity entropy, proposed by Kharzeev and Levin as entanglement between the region probed in deep inelastic scattering and the proton's remainder, was compared with hadron multiplicity data. It is computed from parton densities, which do not fix the partons' quantum state.

items.title: Quantum adversarial physics as a red team framework for physical-layer attacks on quantum cryptographic systems
items.summary: This paper presents a formal adversarial methodology, Quantum Adversarial Physics (QAP), for red teaming quantum cryptographic systems, with a focus on Quantum Key Distribution (QKD) and related quantum protocols. Rather than treating quantum mechanical principles as immutable security guarantees, QAP operationalises them as adversarial variables: coherence times, entanglement correlations, and entropy flows are each reframed as exploitable attack surfaces.

items.title: Comparative Analysis of Classical vs Quantum Secret Sharing Schemes
items.summary: The fundamental concepts, safety guarantees, efficiency, and applicability to real-world cryptographic applications of both classical and quantum secret sharing techniques are carefully discussed in this work. Shamir’s and Blakley’s schemes are examples of CSS schemes that for long have provided information-theoretic security for sharing secrets among multiple parties such that only authorized subsets are able to retrieve the secret.

items.title: Graphics processing unit-accelerated quantum simulation for molecular biology and drug discovery: algorithms, platforms, and emerging applications
items.summary: Artificial intelligence has intensified the need for methods that describe molecular systems with quantum-mechanical accuracy. Gate-based quantum computing offers a principled framework for simulating electronic structure, molecular interactions, and biological processes at a fidelity inaccessible to classical force fields or density functional theory alone, yet scarce, noisy hardware limits direct experimentation.

items.title: From Maps to Metabolism: Historical Precedents and a Unified Critique of Computationalism
items.summary: Alexander Lerchner's recent work on the 'abstraction fallacy' argues that computational functionalism confuses physical processes with abstract descriptions, and that symbolic computation alone cannot instantiate consciousness. Yet these claims were anticipated by Korzybski's map-territory distinction, Searle's critique of strong artificial intelligence, Floridi's levels of abstraction, Spencer et al.'s observer-relativity arguments, Winograd and Flores's account of computation as socially grounded practice, and…

items.title: What is the connection between quantum relationality and symmetry-based relationality?
items.summary: Although it has often been noted that both quantum mechanics and relativistic physics involve significant forms of relationality, the nature of the connection remains unclear. In addressing such a question it makes sense to start from the simplest possibility, so in this article I set out to consider the viability of the hypothesis that the two types of relationality are ultimately the same: that is, quantum states always characterize degrees of freedom which can be changed by a symmetry transformation, so they…

items.title: The Reference System Loophole
items.summary: I argue that the Extended Wigner's Friend theorems have a `loophole' that has previously not been appreciated, coming from the fact that we typically need a reference system to give meaning to a measurement outcome. I show how this loophole can be used in the context of the Local Friendliness theorem to preserve the predictions of quantum mechanics without denying Local Friendliness, and I respond to some objections.

items.title: From Quantum Cryptography to Intuitionism and Beyond: Relativity, Many-Worlds and Non-Locality
items.summary: After a recollection of some of my encounters with Gilles Brassard, on the occasion of his 70th birthday I present, first, a new idea on the creation of new information at a limited rate. Next, I develop the idea that “indeterminacy is relative” and how this illuminates the compatibility between relativity and non-locality.

items.title: Inferring brain structural complexity from dynamical measures
items.summary: Complexity, commonly defined as the coexistence of integration and differentiation, is a fundamental property of thalamocortical networks and is regarded as a prerequisite for adaptive brain function and consciousness. A variety of metrics have been developed to estimate neural complexity from recorded activity and are increasingly employed in both research and clinical settings.

items.title: EL-RAKHAWI TOPOLOGICAL-PHENOMENAL CONSCIOUSNESS RESONANCE SYSTEM (TPCRS) An Objective, Mathematically Closed Framework for Mapping and Quantifying Subjective Experience via Causal Neural Geometry
items.summary: The El-Rakhawi Topological-Phenomenal Consciousness Resonance System (TPCRS) addresses the "Hard Problem of Consciousness" by providing the first mathematically closed framework for objectively quantifying subjective experience. Current neuroscience relies on unreliable behavioral assessments or statistical correlations that cannot distinguish conscious awareness from unconscious processing.
items.source: Zenodo (CERN European Organization for Nuclear Research)

items.title: Quantum Gate Engineering in Superconducting NISQ Platforms: Experimental Methods and Emerging Directions
items.summary: This review aims to provide researchers, experimentalists, and quantum engineers with an updated and technically grounded perspective on the implementation of quantum gates in superconducting NISQ devices. The goal is to establish a comprehensive bridge between theoretical quantum circuit synthesis and its practical, experimental implementation, focusing on superconducting quantum technologies.

items.title: The medium is the message: How neurometabolic entanglement generates conscious experience
items.summary: Most neuroscientific accounts of consciousness assume that conscious experience is constituted by the information conveyed between neurons. The physical-chemical details of the metabolic and physiological processes that convey this information are correspondingly presumed to be relevant only insofar as they support the organization of information processes.

items.title: Exact Syndrome Budgets for Quantum Erasure Recovery
items.summary: We study the number of independent stabilizer syndrome outcomes needed to resolve errors at known erased locations. For every matrix with paired columns, rank r, and maximum independent-pair cardinality ν, we prove the exact profile max |I|=δ rankGI = min{2δ,δ +ν,r}.

items.title: Intrinsic randomness in quantum information theory
items.summary: (English) The unpredictability of quantum physics gives rise to an intrinsic form of randomness. We generate it by performing a measurement on a quantum state. In an adversarial scenario, we then quantify the randomness by the probability that a correlated eavesdropper could correctly guess the measurement outcomes.
items.source: UPCommons institutional repository (Universitat Politècnica de Catalunya)

items.title: UNE COM Fall Research Bulletin October 2026
items.summary: Bulletin including abstracts from the University of New England College of Osteopathic Medicine’s 2026 Fall Research Update and Lightning Talk event.

items.title: Multidimensional revival dynamics in a bosonic many-body system
items.summary: The collapse and revival of localized states in many-body systems is a quintessential example of a quantum interference phenomenon that cannot be explained purely within mean-field theories. Historically, the majority of previous work on quantum revivals has been in a Schrödinger mechanics context, typically for effectively 1D systems with a focus on the autocorrelation function as the key detection observable.

items.title: QSoftCore: A Conceptual Foundation for Quantum Software Engineering
items.summary: Quantum software engineering (QSE) requires understanding application requirements, quantum programs and algorithms, quantum computation paradigms, executions, and deployment. However, relevant quantum computing (QC) concepts are often defined across physical, mathematical, and paradigm-specific levels of abstraction, making it difficult for the QSE community and hence proposed methods to refer to them consistently.

items.title: EXPERIMENTAL PROTOCOL: PRECISION DETECTION OF THE QUANTUM REDUCTION BOUNDARY VIA THE R⁵ LAW, TRAVERSABILITY OF MICRO- WORMHOLES (ER = EPR), AND THE EMERGENCE OF THE THERMODYNAMIC ARROW OF TIME
items.summary: Time-Keeping and Interferometric Synchronization: • Independent atomic clocks based on cold ytterbium ions (¹⁷¹Yb⁺) are mounted adjacent to the external flanges of both the input and output modules. • The time-keeping network is interconnected and synchronized via a frequency comb interferometer using a Pound–Drever–Hall (PDH) loop, achieving a base temporal resolution of σt ≤ 10⁻¹⁸ s.

items.title: Colloquium: Quantum information processing with ensembles of identical particles
items.summary: Identical particles underpin most quantum technologies, but the role of indistinguishability in these processes extends far beyond the symmetrization of many-particle states. This Colloquium presents a unified operational perspective on how particle identity, indistinguishability, exchange statistics, and many-particle interference can instead be harnessed as resources for quantum information processing.

items.title: The Procrustean Body: A Theoretical Analysis of Motion Capture from Critical Disability, Somaesthetic, and Posthuman Perspectives
items.summary: Motion capture (mocap) systems underpin media production and medical science, yet are built on normative assumptions of an ‘ideal’, non-disabled body. This paper presents a theory-led analysis of mocap through critical disability studies, extending prior socio-technical and historical analyses of the technology.
items.source: International ACM SIGACCESS Conference on Computers and Accessibility (ASSETS)

items.title: Effective Noise Thresholds for Reliable Quantum Approximation Optimisation Algorithm under Noisy Environment
items.summary: Variational quantum algorithms are leading candidates for practical utilisation on noisy intermediate-scale quantum (NISQ) processors, but accumulating noise bounds the usefulness of circuit depths. For the quantum approximate optimisation algorithm (QAOA), this trade-off has mostly been addressed by searching for the best depth for a given device.

items.title: Fundamental limits on photonic state preparation from phase-space majorization
items.summary: Preparing complex quantum states of light for quantum information processing tasks often proceeds by converting from simpler states via experimentally accessible operations. We provide fundamental bounds on such probabilistic conversions, both exact and approximate.

items.title: Auditory tracking magnitude, temporal alignment, and anatomical distribution during wakefulness and propofol-based anesthesia
items.summary: Abstract General anesthesia attenuates auditory responses, but response magnitude alone does not describe how residual activity aligns with sound over time or varies across the brain. We jointly characterized these aspects of auditory tracking using stereoelectroencephalography (sEEG) in 13 patients with drug-resistant epilepsy during wakefulness and clinically defined unresponsiveness under propofol-based anesthesia.

items.title: Recursive Corrigibility Framework (Revision 61)
items.summary: The Recursive Corrigibility Framework (RCF) is a correction methodology for claims, theories, arguments and reasoning systems. Corrigibility here means the capacity of a claim, theory, reasoning process or system to expose where it may be wrong, identify which commitments a result actually bears on, and revise those commitments proportionally to the evidence.

items.title: Addiction science needs rehab
items.summary: The science of drug use and addiction faces a crisis of credibility. Despite decades of progress, our field remains disproportionately focused on pathology, risk, and harm, treating ordinary substance use as inherently problematic while devoting comparatively little attention to its functional, pleasurable, and beneficial dimensions.
items.source: The American Journal of Drug and Alcohol Abuse

items.title: The perioperative sensory–cognitive interface: multimodal neuroimaging of hierarchical network reconfiguration in perioperative neurocognitive disorders
items.summary: Perioperative neurocognitive disorders (PNDs) are commonly attributed to neuroinflammation, cerebrovascular stress, anesthetic neurophysiology, and pre-existing brain vulnerability. These mechanisms identify important insults but do not fully explain how they become disturbances of attention, perception, memory, executive control, and fluctuating awareness.

items.title: Synchrony in neural and visceral systems: a bioelectric basis of consciousness
items.summary: The Default Space Theory (DST) of consciousness claims that consciousness arises from bioelectric oscillations across brain and body which become time-locked to form an internal three-dimensionalized "default space" which continuously simulates external reality. Within this frame, we assert that fast rhythms created corticothalamically with the thalamic reticular nucleus (TRN) can become time-locked with regions throughout the brain via nascent oscillations as well as sensory organs and viscera.

items.title: Equilibrium propagation in non-equilibrium quantum systems
items.summary: Equilibrium propagation (EP) is a powerful training algorithm for self-learning physical systems that is widely used for a variety of machine learning inspired tasks. It relies on the existence of an energy function that depends on tunable training parameters, and can be extended to apply to many-body quantum systems in equilibrium.

items.title: PK/PD Modelling of Sevoflurane and Desflurane Effect on the Bispectral Index: A Validation Study in General Anesthesia
items.summary: Abstract Background:: Standard population-based pharmacokinetic and pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) models often fail to account for significant inter-patient variability during general anesthesia, leading to inaccuracies when predicting the depth of hypnosis. This study aims to bridge this personalization gap by developing a patient-specific multi-drug simulator that expands existing interaction models to integrate both intravenous and inhaled anesthetics.

items.title: Top Mysteries of the Mind Revisited: Default Space Theory Eight Years On
items.summary: In 2018 my colleague and I asked five questions that neuroscience had not answered -how subjective experience relates to the physical world, how perception is so fast, how distributed processing yields one experience, why we sleep, and how emotions are regulated -and argued that the Default Space Model supplied insight into each.Eight years on, two of those answers require correction, one has been overtaken by evidence, and the framework behind all five has acquired an internal architecture it did not have.This…

items.title: Directional coordination along the cortical hierarchy is selectively reorganized in schizophrenia
items.summary: Abstract Schizophrenia has long been framed as a disorder of the cortical hierarchy. Yet, the hierarchy has been studied almost entirely as fixed anatomy, leaving its moment-to-moment expression in ongoing brain activity unmeasured.

items.title: Mediated Givenness and Scientific Object-Formation: Infrared and Ultraviolet Radiation Beyond Direct Perception
items.summary: Scientific instruments make imperceptible phenomena knowable, but it remains unclear whether such access enlarges perception itself or only other forms of epistemic availability. This article develops a layered relational realist account of mediated givenness to explain how scientific objects become available without being constituted by human access.
items.source: MetaScientia: Journal of the History and Philosophy of Science

items.title: Identifying neural correlates of auditory perceptual awareness and deviance using a no-report inattentional deafness paradigm
items.summary: Abstract The relationship between neural processes supporting perception, deviance processing, and post-perceptual task demands during auditory processing is not well understood. We used multitone masking and a no-report inattentional deafness paradigm to dissociate neural correlates of auditory perceptual awareness, deviance processing, and task demands.
